bug_semantics: When an administrator runs `fixfiles restore` or the non-full-cleanup path of `fixfiles relabel`, the DEFAULT restore path first has `find` select entries with an unlabeled or undefined SELinux context and then invokes a separate `chcon` process on each pathname. A local attacker controlling a searched directory can replace an intermediate path component with a symlink after `find` checks the entry but before `chcon` resolves the pathname. `chcon --no-dereference` protects only against dereferencing a symlink in the final pathname component; it does not prevent traversal through a swapped intermediate symlink, so the privileged process can change the SELinux label of an arbitrary target such as `/etc/shadow`.
flaw_origin: The vulnerable find-then-chcon mechanism predates the repository's accessible Git history. The earliest relevant Git object, root commit 13cd4c8960688af11ad23b4c946149015c80d549, is explicitly an `initial import from svn trunk revision 2950` and already contains the `/tmp` and `/var/tmp` find/chcon commands. It has no parent and aggregates the prior Subversion history, so it is not the smallest BIC. Later commits changed details without creating the race: 5bd734dd7395a2f6c87546b8e7159b02544405f9 replaced hard-coded label types with `chcon --reference`, and 2608b4d6660af0fb8ad93f2cc144bdaab3c2afa8 added `--no-dereference` but retained the separate pathname lookup. The pre-r2950 Subversion changeset that first introduced the mechanism and its immediate predecessor are not present in the validated clone and could not be reconstructed from the available upstream history.
ai_marker: unavailable: the true smallest BIC is behind the pre-r2950 Subversion-history boundary, so there is no BIC commit object in the validated Git clone on which to check author, committer, Co-Authored-By/Generated-with trailers, or bot identity; the human-authored 13cd4c8960688af11ad23b4c946149015c80d549 import object was inspected only to establish the boundary and is not treated as the BIC
evidence: The bundle's first-party GHSA description and Red Hat CNA page https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/CVE-2026-19079 identify CWE-367 in policycoreutils/scripts/fixfiles: a local attacker races the find/chcon pathname handoff while an administrator runs restore or relabel; Red Hat states that the vulnerable cleanup path has been present for many years.

`git show --format=fuller a556538c2d5d2583273e025b45c02651fef47679` shows Stephen Smalley's direct upstream fix, `policycoreutils/scripts/fixfiles: drop /tmp cleanup`. Its patch deletes the vulnerable find/chcon block from policycoreutils/scripts/fixfiles, and its message explicitly explains that chcon re-looks up the full pathname and is subject to TOCTOU. `git rev-parse a556538c2d5d2583273e025b45c02651fef47679^` resolves the fix parent to 7fd20e48504069fe1541f809de7566283f8ec7db.

At 7fd20e48504069fe1541f809de7566283f8ec7db, policycoreutils/scripts/fixfiles lines in `restore()` show DEFAULT-mode find commands for /tmp, /var/tmp, /var/run, and /var/lib/debug executing `chcon --no-dereference --reference` on pathnames. The `process()` dispatch maps `restore` to `restore Relabel`; `relabel()` also reaches `restore Relabel` when /tmp is not fully deleted, proving the advisory attack path.

`git log -L 288,302:policycoreutils/scripts/fixfiles a556538c2d5d2583273e025b45c02651fef47679^` traces the vulnerable block through 2608b4d6660af0fb8ad93f2cc144bdaab3c2afa8 (2017 addition of `--no-dereference`), 5bd734dd7395a2f6c87546b8e7159b02544405f9 (2011 conversion to `--reference`), and ultimately 13cd4c8960688af11ad23b4c946149015c80d549, where the commands are already present in the newly imported file.

`git show --no-patch --format=raw 13cd4c8960688af11ad23b4c946149015c80d549` shows no parent header and the message `initial import from svn trunk revision 2950`; therefore direct parent-tree absence cannot be verified and this aggregate import cannot serve as the protocol's smallest BIC.

Version boundary: annotated component tag policycoreutils-3.11 resolves to 2233a23a4d4f1bf29054037babec13f30d038e65 and its policycoreutils/scripts/fixfiles still contains all four vulnerable find/chcon commands. `git merge-base --is-ancestor policycoreutils-3.11 a556538c2d5d2583273e025b45c02651fef47679` succeeds, while `git tag --contains a556538c2d5d2583273e025b45c02651fef47679` returns no tags. Thus upstream 3.11 is vulnerable and the direct fix lands later on main, with no patched upstream release tag in the validated history; the advisory bundle itself supplies no formal package-version ranges.
reasoning: The vulnerability is the non-atomic pathname handoff between `find` and privileged `chcon`, not the final-component symlink behavior alone. That is why the 2017 `--no-dereference` change is neither the origin nor a complete fix: an attacker can still swap an intermediate directory component. The lifecycle visible in Git begins with the already-vulnerable 2008 SVN snapshot, continues through label-selection and symlink-hardening edits that preserve the mechanism, is present in policycoreutils-3.11, and ends when a556538c2d5d2583273e025b45c02651fef47679 directly deletes the obsolete cleanup block. Protocol forbids treating an import aggregate as the BIC. Because the root object says it imported SVN revision 2950, has no parent, and already contains the flaw, the smallest causal commit and parent-absence proof lie in unavailable pre-import Subversion history. Without that BIC commit object, BIC-only AI attribution cannot be performed; neither the import object's identity nor later commits may substitute. This is therefore BLOCKED by a genuine public-history boundary rather than EVIDENCE_GAP or a closed NOT_AI judgment.
remaining_gap: Obtain the upstream Subversion history before trunk revision 2950, identify the exact changeset that first added the separate find/chcon relabel mechanism, verify those lines are absent in its immediate predecessor tree, and inspect that true BIC's author/committer-equivalent metadata and message/trailers. Until that history is available, introducer_sha, introducer_parent, parent absence, squash decomposition, and BIC-only AI attribution cannot be established.
